investigation.name: 1MDB
investigation.question: How was money raised by Malaysia's state fund 1MDB between 2009 and 2014 diverted, through which companies, banks and people, and who has been held to account for it?
investigation.description: A demo investigation of the 1MDB scandal built only from 11 public records: US Justice Department complaints, the Low/Ng indictment, Leissner's criminal information, Goldman Sachs's 2020 deferred prosecution agreement, a Federal Reserve order, and Singapore (MAS) and Swiss (FINMA) regulator releases. Facts in the DOJ civil forfeiture complaints are allegations unless a guilty plea, an admitted statement of facts or a regulator finding supports them.

entities.caption: 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB)
entities.note: Malaysian state investment fund wholly owned by the Ministry of Finance; formed 2009 from Terengganu Investment Authority.

evidence.quote: 1Malaysia Development Berhad (“1MDB”) was a strategic investment and development company wholly owned by the Government of Malaysia through its Ministry of Finance (“MOF”).
In September 2009, TIA’s name was changed to 1Malaysia Development Berhad, or 1MDB.

entities.caption: Terengganu Investment Authority (TIA)
entities.note: Predecessor of 1MDB; Jho Low advised on its creation.

evidence.quote: In or around February 2009, the Malaysian municipality of Terengganu, assisted by Goldman, formed TIA with the stated purpose of investing and managing that municipality’s public funds.

entities.caption: 1MDB Global Investments Limited
entities.note: 1MDB subsidiary that issued the $3 billion Project Catalyze bond in March 2013.

evidence.quote: The bonds were issued by 1MDB Global Investments Limited (“1MDB Global”), a wholly- owned subsidiary of 1MDB that was incorporated in the British Virgin Islands on March 8, 2013.

entities.caption: 1MDB Energy Limited
entities.note: 1MDB subsidiary that issued the $1.75bn Project Magnolia notes (May 2012) to buy Tanjong Energy.

evidence.quote: The offering circular for the Project Magnolia bonds, dated May 18, 2012, indicates that 1MDB Energy issued $1.75 billion in privately-placed notes, with an interest rate of 5.99% per annum, redeemable in 2022.

entities.caption: 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited
entities.note: 1MDB subsidiary created 13 Aug 2012 to hold the Genting power assets and issue the Project Maximus bonds.

evidence.quote: another wholly-owned subsidiary called “1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited” (“1MDB Energy Langat”), for the purposes of holding the power assets and issuing debt securities

entities.caption: 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited (1MEHL)
entities.note: 1MDB power-assets holding company; borrower of the 2014 Deutsche Bank loans used for the "options buyback".

evidence.quote: On or about May 26, 2014, Deutsche Bank AG, Singapore Branch extended a $250 million bridge loan facility to 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited (“$250 million loan”).

entities.caption: 1MDB PetroSaudi Ltd. (joint venture)
entities.note: Purported 2009 joint venture: 1MDB 40% for $1bn cash, PetroSaudi 60% for claimed energy concessions.

evidence.quote: 1MDB PetroSaudi, Ltd. was a purported joint venture between 1MDB and PetroSaudi formed in or around September 2009 for the stated purpose of exploiting certain energy concessions PetroSaudi purportedly owned in Turkmenistan and Argentina.

entities.caption: Abu Dhabi Malaysia Investment Company (ADMIC)
entities.note: Purported 50:50 1MDB–Aabar joint venture that the 2013 Catalyze bond was meant to fund; never capitalized.

evidence.quote: Abu Dhabi Malaysia Investment Company (“ADMIC”) is a purported joint venture between 1MDB and Aabar that was created in or around March 2013 for the stated purpose of promoting the growth and development of Malaysia and Abu Dhabi. It was never capitalized.

entities.caption: PetroSaudi International Ltd.
entities.note: Private Saudi oil services company, 1MDB's 2009 joint-venture partner.

evidence.quote: PetroSaudi International Ltd. (“PetroSaudi” or “PSI”) is a private Saudi Arabia-based oil services company incorporated in Saudi Arabia, which maintains offices in the United Kingdom.

address: P.O. Box 1239, Offshore Incorporation, Victoria, Mahe, Republic of Seychelles
name: Good Star Limited

entities.note: Seychelles company that received $1.03bn of 1MDB joint-venture money; alleged to be controlled by Jho Low.

evidence.quote: RBS Coutts bank account records indicate that Good Star Limited was formed in the Seychelles on or about May 18, 2009.

Deutsche Bank submitted to RBS Coutts a revised SWIFT instruction identifying “Good Star Limited” as the beneficiary of the $700 million wire transfer, located at P.O. Box 1239, Offshore Incorporation, Victoria, Mahe, Republic of Seychelles.

entities.caption: Smart Power

evidence.quote: The sole director of Good Star is listed as Smart Power, of which LOW is the sole director.

entities.caption: International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC)
entities.note: Abu Dhabi sovereign investment fund; guaranteed the 2012 1MDB bonds. ("Foreign Agency A" in the criminal filings.)

evidence.quote: International Petroleum Investment Company (“IPIC”) was an investment fund wholly owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi.

entities.caption: Aabar Investments PJS
entities.note: The real Abu Dhabi company, an IPIC subsidiary ("Foreign Investment Firm A" in the criminal filings).

evidence.quote: Aabar Investments PJS (“Aabar”) was a private joint stock company incorporated under the laws of Abu Dhabi, and a subsidiary of IPIC.

entities.caption: Aabar Investments PJS Limited (BVI)
entities.note: BVI look-alike of Aabar that received about $1.367bn of 2012 bond proceeds; IPIC and Aabar say it is not theirs.

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Incumbency prepared by Aabar-BVI’s registered agent in the BVI indicates that Aabar-BVI was incorporated in BVI on March 14, 2012.
Aabar-BVI was created and named to give the impression that it was associated with Aabar Investments PJS (“Aabar”), a subsidiary of IPIC incorporated in Abu Dhabi.

entities.caption: Aabar Investments PJS Limited (Seychelles)
entities.note: Second look-alike, incorporated May 2014 by Husseiny; received about $681m of the 2014 Deutsche Bank loan.

evidence.quote: one incorporated in the Seychelles5 in May 2014 by HUSSEINY (“Aabar- Seychelles”). Aabar-BVI maintained a bank account at BSI Bank in Switzerland, and Aabar-Seychelles maintained a bank account at UBS AG in Singapore.

entities.caption: UBS AG

evidence.quote: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced today that it has served BSI Bank Limited (BSI Bank) notice of intention to withdraw its status as a merchant bank in Singapore

entities.caption: Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA)

claims.text: Goldman underwrote three bond offerings in 2012 and 2013 that raised about $6.5 billion for 1MDB and earned it more than $600 million in fees and revenue.
claims.rationale: Admitted by Goldman in the DPA Statement of Facts; consistent with the Federal Reserve order and Leissner's information.

evidence.quote: three bond offerings that were related to 1MDB’s energy acquisitions and that raised a total of approximately $6.5 billion for 1MDB in 2012 and 2013.
ultimately earned Goldman in excess of $600 million in fees and revenue across its divisions, and increased Goldman’s stature in Southeast Asia.
Goldman Sachs International, a London-based subsidiary of GS Group, served as the sole arranger and underwriter of three bond offerings

claims.text: Goldman admitted conspiring to provide about $1.6 billion to, or for the benefit of, foreign officials and their relatives to win 1MDB business.
claims.rationale: Admitted in the DPA Statement of Facts, which Goldman stipulated is true and accurate.

evidence.quote: In total, Goldman conspired to provide approximately $1.6077 billion to, or for the benefit of, foreign officials and their relatives, of which approximately $18.1 million was paid from accounts controlled by Leissner.
Goldman hereby agrees and stipulates that the following facts and conclusions of law are true and accurate.

claims.text: Leissner falsely told Goldman's control committees that Jho Low was not involved in the bond deals.
claims.rationale: Admitted by Goldman in the DPA and pleaded to by Leissner (overt act in the information to which he pleaded guilty).

evidence.quote: Ng was also present during this meeting and did not correct Leissner’s false statement about Low’s involvement.
LEISSNER told the committee affirmatively that Co-Conspirator #1 was not involved in Project Maximus, though he knew that this statement was false at the time

claims.text: A day after Project Magnolia closed, about $577 million of the proceeds went to a BVI company named to look like Aabar but not associated with it.
claims.rationale: Admitted in the DPA (with anonymized labels); the civil complaints give the same amount, date and name the company Aabar-BVI.

evidence.quote: However, Shell Company 1 was not, in fact, associated with Aabar but was rather associated with Abu Dhabi Official 1, Abu Dhabi Official 2 and Low.

Roughly one day later, on or about May 22, 2012, a wire in the amount of $576,943,490 was sent from 1MDB Energy’s bank account at Falcon Bank to an account at BSI Bank in Lugano, Switzerland maintained by Aabar-BVI

claims.text: About $681 million of Project Catalyze money reached an account of Malaysian Official 1 in March 2013.
claims.rationale: Admitted in the DPA Statement of Facts ($620m + $61m to Malaysian Official 1); the 2017 civil complaint traces the same sums from the Tanore account.

evidence.quote: On or about March 21, 2013, approximately $620 million was transferred from a shell entity beneficially owned or controlled by Low, Shell Company Account 7, to an account beneficially owned and controlled by Malaysian Official 1.
On or about March 25, 2013, an additional $61,000,000 was wired from the Tanore Account to the same account at AmBank, for a total of $681,000,000.

claims.text: Malaysian Official 1 received about $30 million of Project Maximus proceeds in October and November 2012.
claims.rationale: Admitted in the DPA; the 2017 civil complaint shows Blackstone paying $5m and $25m on the same dates to the AMPRIVATE BANKING-MR account.

evidence.quote: Between on or about October 30, 2012 and on or about November 19, 2012, approximately $30 million was transferred from Shell Company Account 2 to an account held by Malaysian Official 1.
Blackstone transferred $25,000,000 to the same AMPRIVATE BANKING-MR Account belonging to MALAYSIAN OFFICIAL 1.

claims.text: Leissner routed about $4.1 million in 2014 to a New York jeweler, partly to pay for jewelry for the wife of Malaysian Official 1.
claims.rationale: Admitted in the DPA and an overt act in the information to which Leissner pleaded guilty.

evidence.quote: On or about October 10, 2014, Leissner caused approximately $4.1 million to be transferred from Management Company 1 Account to Jeweler 1 in New York, New York, in part to pay for approximately $1.3 million in jewelry
On or about October 10, 2014, LEISSNER caused approximately $4.1 million to be wire transferred from a foreign bank account controlled by

claims.text: Jho Low was the beneficial owner of Good Star Limited, the company that received $1.03 billion meant for the PetroSaudi joint venture.
claims.rationale: Alleged in the DOJ civil forfeiture complaints (2016, 2017, 2025), citing bank records; not admitted or adjudicated in this document set.

evidence.quote: According to banking records, Good Star was a company controlled by LOW, and LOW was also the Good Star Account’s beneficial owner and sole authorized signatory.
Contrary to representations made by 1MDB officials, the Good Star Account was beneficially owned not by PetroSaudi or the joint venture, but by LOW Taek Jho, a/k/a Jho Low (“LOW”)

In total, 1MDB purported to invest a total of $1.83 billion in the 1MDB- PetroSaudi Joint Venture through a combination of equity and debt investments. Of this amount, $1.03 billion was fraudulently diverted to the Good Star Account.

claims.text: Aabar-BVI sent $238 million to Riza Aziz's Red Granite Capital, money that helped fund Red Granite Pictures and "The Wolf of Wall Street".
claims.rationale: Alleged in the 2017 civil complaint. The DPA admits about $60m went from a shell account to "U.S. Motion Picture Company 1" (part-owned by a relative of Malaysian Official 1) to finance films, but does not name Red Granite.

evidence.quote: Aabar-BVI also transferred $238,000,000 to a Singapore bank account belonging to Red Granite Capital, an entity owned by Riza Shahriz Bin Abdul AZIZ (“AZIZ”).

Between on or about June 20, 2012 and on or about November 20, 2012, approximately $60 million was transferred over multiple wires from Shell Company Account 3 to the account of U.S. Motion Picture Company 1

claims.text: Khadem al-Qubaisi received $472.75 million of 2012 bond money through the Blackstone account.
claims.rationale: Alleged in the 2017 civil complaint. The DPA and indictment admit/charge the same total ($258.75m + $214m) going to an account of "Abu Dhabi Official 1" but never name him.

evidence.quote: Blackstone transferred $472,750,000 into a Luxembourg account beneficially owned by QUBAISI.

approximately $258.75 million was transferred via wire from Shell Company Account 2 to an account at Foreign Financial Institution B in the name of Shell Company Account 4, which was beneficially owned and controlled by Abu Dhabi Official 1.

claims.text: Jho Low used more than $250 million diverted from 1MDB to buy the superyacht Equanimity.
claims.rationale: Alleged in the 2017 civil forfeiture complaint; no admission or judgment in this set.

evidence.quote: between January 7, 2014, and June 3, 2014, over $250 million in funds diverted from 1MDB was funneled into the World View Account in four major tranches for the purpose of acquiring and maintaining THE EQUANIMITY.

claims.text: 1MDB general counsel Jasmine Loo received 1MDB money and used $3.1 million of it to buy a London property.
claims.rationale: Alleged in the 2017 and 2019 civil complaints only.

evidence.quote: More than $3 million from the 2013 1MDB bond offering was diverted into an account of LOO and used to purchase property in London, United Kingdom owned by Red Mountain Global Ltd.
On or about December 6, 2012, a wire in the amount of $5,000,000 was sent from the Blackstone Account to an account at Falcon Bank in Zurich maintained in the name of River Dee International SA

claims.text: 1MDB officials made the $700 million transfer of September 2009 to PetroSaudi as settlement of amounts the joint venture owed it.
claims.rationale: This is what 1MDB OFFICER 2 told the 1MDB board (as quoted in the civil complaint); the complaint's bank records show the money went to Good Star, which it alleges Low controlled.

evidence.quote: US$700 million was remitted to PSI directly as settlement of all the amounts owed by the JVCo. to PSI.
This payment was for beneficiary ‘Good Star Limited’ in their SWIFT. Good Star is owned 100% by PetroSaudi International Limited.
J.P. Morgan Chase bank records confirm that on or about September 30, 2009, the Good Star Account received the $700 million wire transfer from Deutsche Bank.
As detailed below, the $700 million went to an account controlled by LOW, not by PetroSaudi.

claims.text: The $681 million that reached Malaysian Official 1's account was a personal donation from the Saudi royal family.
claims.rationale: Malaysia's Attorney General's characterisation (as quoted in the 2017 complaint) conflicts with Goldman's admission in the DPA and the complaint's bank records showing bond proceeds via Tanore/Shell Company Account 7.

evidence.quote: The Malaysian Attorney General ultimately characterized the payment of $681 million as a “personal donation to [MALAYSIAN OFFICIAL 1] from the Saudi royal family which was given to him without any consideration.”
official bank records for the Tanore Account confirm that (a) the payment of $681 million came from the Tanore Account; (b) TAN was the recorded beneficial owner of the Tanore Account

On or about March 21, 2013, approximately $620 million was transferred from a shell entity beneficially owned or controlled by Low, Shell Company Account 7, to an account beneficially owned and controlled by Malaysian Official 1.

claims.text: The $1.367 billion 1MDB paid to Aabar-BVI in 2012 was a refundable deposit held as collateral for IPIC's guarantee.
claims.rationale: 1MDB's audited accounts booked it as a refundable deposit; the same complaint says bankers were told the payments were non-refundable, the contribution agreements let Aabar-BVI use the cash as it saw fit, and IPIC/Aabar deny Aabar-BVI is theirs.

evidence.quote: In their audited financial statements for the year ending on March 31, 2014, 1MDB booked their substantial payments to Aabar-BVI as an asset rather than a payment

In contrast, LOW and 1MDB officers represented to bank officials involved in the transfer of the $1.367 billion that the funds represented non-refundable payments to Aabar-BVI in consideration of IPIC’s guarantee of the 2012 bonds.
This characterization is inconsistent with the terms of the two Contribution Agreements that were provided to BSI to justify the payments.

claims.text: Aabar Investments PJS Limited (BVI) was owned by IPIC's subsidiary Aabar.
claims.rationale: The BVI incumbency certificate and a 1MDB press release say so; IPIC and Aabar told the London Stock Exchange it was not in their group; the DPA admits the shell was not associated with Aabar.

evidence.quote: That certificate lists QUBAISI and HUSSEINY as Aabar-BVI’s Directors and “Aabar Investments PJS” as its sole shareholder.
1MDB company records show documentary evidence of the ownership of Aabar BVI and of each payment made
In that statement, IPIC and Aabar stated that, “Aabar BVI was not an entity within either corporate group”
However, Shell Company 1 was not, in fact, associated with Aabar but was rather associated with Abu Dhabi Official 1, Abu Dhabi Official 2 and Low.

claims.text: Husseiny invested his own personal money in Red Granite Pictures.
claims.rationale: Aziz (to the New York Times) and Husseiny's attorney said so, as quoted in the 2017 complaint; the complaint says the money came from Aabar-BVI, i.e. 1MDB bond proceeds, and that Aziz told his accountants part was a "gift".

evidence.quote: an attorney for HUSSEINY is quoted as saying that HUSSEINY’s investment in Red Granite was made with “personal money.”

The funds sent from Aabar-BVI to Red Granite Capital, which were thereafter transferred into the United States for use by Red Granite Pictures, did not represent a legitimate investment by 1MDB, IPIC, or Aabar in Red Granite Pictures.
AZIZ claimed that this money was a “gift” from Aabar-BVI, including in documentation provided to his accountants in connection with the preparation of his 2012 U.S. tax return.

claims.text: In 2014, 1MDB agreed to pay $989 million to buy back the options it had granted Aabar.
claims.rationale: The figure comes from the agreement shown to BSI and Deutsche Bank's understanding; in the same documents the Settlement Agreement left the price open and the version shown to UBS said $2.45 billion (all as described in the 2017 complaint).

evidence.quote: would assign its rights to the Aabar options to 1MEHL in exchange for $989,000,000, of which $175,000,000 was payable within 30 days of the date of the agreement.
The parties did not fix the price for the buyback in the Settlement Agreement but instead provided that 1MDB would pay a “price . . . to be mutually agreed between the parties” at a later date.
HUSSEINY represented to UBS that 1MEHL had agreed to pay Aabar-Seychelles $2.45 billion to terminate the Aabar options.

claims.text: Malaysian Official 1 was Malaysia's prime minister at the time of the bond deals.
claims.rationale: Every document uses only the label and a role (high-ranking official in the executive branch and Ministry of Finance with authority over 1MDB). The DPA records Leissner describing a letter he carried as "by the Prime Minister of Malaysia" and elsewhere as a letter from Malaysian Official 1; that is an inference, not an identification. Needs an outside primary source.

claims.text: Malaysian courts have convicted people over the 1MDB diversions described in these filings.
claims.rationale: No Malaysian court judgment is in this document set; it must be obtained separately before any statement is made.

claims.text: The assets named in the US forfeiture complaints, including the Equanimity, were recovered and returned to Malaysia after 2025.
claims.rationale: The set ends with the January 2025 complaint; it contains no forfeiture judgments, settlements or repatriation records.

claims.text: "Abu Dhabi Official 1" and "Abu Dhabi Official 2" in the DPA are Khadem al-Qubaisi and Mohamed al-Husseiny.
claims.rationale: The amounts and dates match the named flows in the civil complaints, but the DPA never names them; the link is an inference, not a documented fact.

leads.title: Obtain the SEC administrative order against Goldman (Oct 2020)
leads.detail: The DPA cites an SEC settlement ($606m disgorgement, $400m penalty). The order's findings are not in this set and may describe the bond deals and controls in more detail.

leads.title: Map the DPA's anonymized accounts to the named entities
leads.detail: Shell Company Accounts 1-8, Holding Company 2 and Management Company 1 (DPA) line up by amount and date with Aabar-BVI, Blackstone, Vasco, Tanore and others in the civil complaints. Confirm each link with court exhibits, Leissner's and Ng's trial record, or bank records before treating them as the same.

leads.title: Pull the Leissner plea transcript and the Roger Ng trial record
leads.detail: Leissner pleaded guilty on 28 Aug 2018 (Fed order). The transcript, sentencing papers and Ng trial exhibits would turn civil-complaint allegations (Red Granite, Qubaisi payments) into tested evidence.

leads.title: Track the outcome of each forfeiture case
leads.detail: Check dockets CV 16-5371 (Park Laurel), CV 17-4441 (Equanimity), CV 19-1326 (London property) and 2:25-cv-00474 ($20m UBS/Fidelity) for consent judgments, claimants and where the money went.

leads.title: Singapore prosecutions of BSI and Falcon staff
leads.detail: MAS referred six BSI staff (incl. Hans Peter Brunner and Yeo Jiawei) and reported Falcon branch manager Jens Sturzenegger's arrest. Obtain Singapore court outcomes and the Raffles Money Change referral result.

leads.title: FINMA proceedings against two former BSI top managers
leads.detail: FINMA opened individual proceedings in May 2016 and the Swiss Attorney General opened criminal proceedings. Find the outcomes and whether the managers are named.

leads.title: Identify "Individual 1" in the 2025 complaint
leads.detail: Their company got $20m from Husseiny's MB Consulting and a $69m buyout of a 2013 infrastructure joint venture with 1MDB. The complaint says Individual 1 did not know the source; check the stipulation filed with it and Malaysian records of the joint venture.

leads.title: IPIC and Aabar filings on the look-alike entities
leads.detail: Obtain IPIC's 11 April 2016 London Stock Exchange statement and its 2015 consolidated accounts, which say other offshore "Aabar" entities exist and that IPIC paid $103m of 1MDB bond interest.
